body:
Received, thank you. This request is tracked in this repository as import bead `think-t6ok`.

The import will:

- **Retain** the source at evand/square-packing `13ee36e5807727d12a5da36b9b90a96bdba272bf`, `s12/search/exact/`, as a packet in this repository: the 48 certificates below the register, both checkers, `results.md` and the READMEs kept byte for byte, and the other files pinned by digest.
- **Replay** the certificates here, with your `verify_cert.py` and `verify_cert2.py` as retained and with this repository's own exact checkers, and compare each certified side and pose with what the register holds.
- **Review** the claim in a separately prompted adversarial review.

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

Thank you again for this. Here is where the import stands. **Everything below is recorded on an intake branch of this repository and has not been merged to `main`.** The id is provisional until the merge, and a reply from `main` will follow.

**Registered.** T-098, at V3/C3 (confirmed): s(n) ≤ S' at the 48 counts you listed, where S' is the rational side of your certificate at `13ee36e`. Each case record now carries S', written out in full, as both its reported and its verified upper bound.

- At n = 126 the verified ceiling is no longer the 12 × 12 grid.
- At n = 206, 259, 305 and 306 the verified ceiling no longer trails the reported side.
- T-057 and T-092, whose counts all lie among the 48, now read as superseded.
- The known-best witness each record lists, which the atlas pictures, stays the finder's binary64 pose. The certificate is the witness of the side.

**Replayed here.** Every certificate except n = 17 (320 in all):

- **Decided by this repository's checkers.** Each certificate was converted to exact rationals without rounding and decided by two checkers that share no code with each other or with yours: `sqpack`'s exact separating-axis test and an independent rational-corner checker. Both accept all 320, in 2,820 CPU seconds on two workers.
- **Your checkers.** `verify_cert.py` and `verify_cert2.py` were run as retained, each held to its exit status and its last line. Both accept all 320, in 202 CPU seconds.
- **Controls, at each of the 48.** Two altered copies were made: one with the tightest pair moved one unit of the side's denominator past touching, and one with the box shrunk by its least clearance plus that unit. All four checkers refuse both.
- **Against the register.** Each S' lies 3.5e-13 (n = 211) to 5.0e-11 (n = 270) below the printed side. Matched square for square, every certificate lies within 1.441e-3 of the known-best witness. Every square you do not list as free lies within 4.2e-5 of it.
- **Your solver.** `exactsolve.py` was run on five pinned inputs (n = 68, 102, 126, 211, 270), taking 178 CPU seconds. Each regenerated certificate has exactly the retained S' and decides valid here. None is byte-identical to the retained file, which is what `reproduce.sh` tests: centres differ by at most 2.5e-24 and tangents by at most 3.3e-24.

**One thing in the batch you may want to fix.** `verify_all.sh` tests the last line of `verify_cert.py` with `grep -q VALID`, and `INVALID` matches that too. So that leg cannot report a failure. On an overlapped copy of n = 68 the script printed `verify_cert2 FAIL` and never `verify_cert FAIL`. `summarize.py` uses the same test (`'VALID' in` the last line). Run here and held to its exit status, `verify_cert.py` does accept all 320, so nothing in the claim depends on this.

**Recorded as reported, not verified.** That 44 of the 48 exact points are KKT local minima. This concerns the packings, not s(n), and nothing here checks it.

**Not registered.**

- **The other 272 certificates**, as you asked. They were replayed with the 48 and are pinned by digest. At the 78 counts whose verified ceiling trails the reported side they could carry that ceiling. You did not ask for that use, so it is held for the owner's decision.
- **The n = 17 certificate.** The owner is holding it for separate n = 17 work. It was not imported, replayed or recorded.

**Review.** A separately prompted adversarial review found the bound sound. Its one blocking defect was in our own records, not in your work: n = 126 kept the catalogue's conjectured optimum, which lies above the ceiling your certificate verifies. That is fixed, and the records now refuse such a conjecture. A second separately prompted reviewer checked the fixes the same day and found the blocking defect resolved; what it left open is non-blocking. Neither reviewer could run code, so the next review, the one a higher rung needs, should decide some certificates with code of its own.

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

@evand, the records described in the reply above are now merged to `main` (#369): **T-098 at V3/C3**. At the 48 counts both upper lanes are at your certified sides, and T-057 and T-092 are superseded.

Your n = 105 note, a first-order descent of about -2.8e-6 per unit step once corner-to-corner touches may slip, so possibly not a local minimum: it is recorded as reported, not registered. The record keeps n = 105's witness and upper bound as they were; nothing here confirms or refutes the descent.

[`results.yaml` (T-098)](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/packing/frontier/results.yaml), [the review](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/docs/project/reviews/review-2026-10-06-evand-exact-optima.md) and [the fix check](https://github.com/jlevy/squares/blob/main/docs/project/reviews/review-2026-10-06-evand-exact-optima-fix-check.md).

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

@evand, thank you again. In this issue you offered the rest of your certificates as an independent exact replay of existing upper bounds, and asked for nothing. We have used them where they lower this register's verified upper bound, recorded as T-101 (V3/C3).

**What changed.** At 77 counts from n = 28 to 300, s(n) ≤ S', your certificate's side. Each case record carries S' rounded up at the fourteen decimals the Kingbird catalogue prints, as its verified upper bound.

- **74 of these were the integer grid,** up to 0.464 above the printed side.
- **At n = 69, 83 and 87** they were our own certificates from a parse of the catalogue's pictures (T-088 and T-089). Those are now superseded as bounds; the packings remain the best known.
- **At 22 counts** the verified bound now agrees with the printed side to one unit in its last place.
- **At the 55 counts where the catalogue gives a closed form,** your S' lies 7.6e-20 to 1.8e-19 above it. Six of those forms are rational (n = 50, 171, 198, 230, 261 and 293). At n = 50 your exact point before scaling looks like a rational packing at exactly 53/7, and we have opened a follow-up for it.
- **n = 29 is unchanged:** an interval-certified bound there already sits 5e-21 below your S'.

**How they were checked.** All 77 were accepted in the 5 October replay by both of this repository's exact checkers and both of yours. Three altered copies of each were checked, and each was refused or accepted exactly as it should be. The 77 certificates are retained in our packet at 13ee36e.

Two separately prompted reviews, a review and a fix check, found the bound sound. The one blocking point was our own wording about closed forms, now fixed. Neither reviewer could run code. The n = 17 certificate remains held for the n = 17 work.

_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

Update: n = 105 and 130 are now certified too (323 of 324; only n = 292 remains open), pushed in commit [7eef24f](https://github.com/evand/square-packing/tree/7eef24f/s12/search/exact/batch).

| n | S' (certificate) | register | difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| 105 | 10.806077865519704632682966129102 | 10.806077865540567 | −2.09e-11 |
| 130 | 11.911187706535762355657987890878 | 11.911187706548755 | −1.30e-11 |

Files: `certs/n-105.cert`, `certs/n-130.cert`, `inputs/n-105.txt`, `inputs/n-130.txt`. Both pass `verify_cert.py` and `verify_cert2.py`. As before, these are exact optima of Couzo's packings, not new packings.

Two solver fixes made this possible (both described in `batch/README.md`):
- **n = 130:** near convergence, the Jacobian of the KKT Newton solve turned singular, because the independent contact subset chosen at the f64 input became dependent. `exactsolve.py` now re-chooses that subset at the current point.
- **n = 105:** as noted above, the register witness is not a local minimum: there is a first-order descent once corner–corner touches may slip. The certificate is solved from the witness after a local squeeze, then treated with one branch's corner–corner touches as equations. In that branch it is a KKT local minimum. The certificate proves only the upper bound.

The squeeze optimizer mentioned above ("not yet published") is now in the same repository, under `s12/search/packer/`.

Update: n = 292 is now certified too, which makes 324 of 324.

| n | S' (certificate) | register | difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| 292 | 17.597249391156465040647414499422 | 17.597249391199519 | −4.31e-11 |

Files: `s12/search/exact/batch/certs/n-292.cert` and `inputs/n-292.txt` at f58a017 (solve log:
`s12/search/packer/s292.md`). Both `verify_cert.py` and `verify_cert2.py` accept it. This is the exact optimum of
Couzo's packing, not a new packing. It is a strict local minimum modulo 119 exact flat motions on the same numerical evidence as the others
(min λ 2.15e-4), and jammed in every corner–corner branch.

Why it failed before: one corner square (square 0) sat about 1e-6 rad off axis with its corner on a neighbour's corner.
That gave a spurious load path and a nearly singular contact subset (σ_min 1.9e-7), so the projection step stalled.
Setting that square to 0° in the input fixes it, and exactsolve converges in 5 steps.

We also ran about 390 local quenches and cold chains from the record and from older packings: nothing below it.

Thanks for catching the `verify_all.sh` bug. `INVALID` matched `grep -q VALID`, so the `verify_cert.py` leg could never fail. It is fixed at [cca7bf1](https://github.com/evand/square-packing/commit/cca7bf1). The script now matches the exact verdict line, `^  VALID:`, and `summarize.py` matches with `startswith('VALID:')`. A re-run gives 324 of 324 valid under both verifiers, and an `INVALID` line is now rejected.

Since #419, itsnaka's SQUISH packings (#401) have superseded the records at n = 108, 123, 126, 129, 130, 153–155, 179, 180, 208, 209, 237–239, 258, 263 and 303. Our certificates at those n are still valid upper bounds, but they no longer give the best ones.
